instructions: The night before, or at least 4 hours ahead: in a large bowl, stir together the 2 cups oats, 2 cups milk, 1 cup Greek yogurt, 1/4 cup chia seeds, 1/4 cup maple syrup, 2 tsp vanilla, 1 tsp cinnamon and a pinch of salt. Keep stirring until there are no dry pockets of oats or lumps of yogurt left.
Spoon it into 4 jars or containers with lids, about 1 cup in each. Seal them and put them in the fridge.

In the morning, put the 1/2 cup walnuts in a dry skillet over medium heat. Toast them for 3 to 4 minutes, shaking the pan now and then, until they smell toasty and turn a shade darker. Transfer them onto a board and chop them roughly.
Open the jars and give each one a good stir. The oats will have soaked up the milk and gone thick and soft.
Split the blueberries between the jars and scatter the walnuts over the top.
Serve cold, straight from the jar. Any jars you don't eat keep in the fridge for up to 3 days.
advance_prep_notes: Mix the oats and put them in jars the night before (at least 4 hours ahead).
method_notes: All three soak rolled oats in about an equal volume of milk with yogurt, chia seeds and a little maple syrup or honey, then chill them. Downshiftology (the lead) uses 1/2 cup each of oats and milk per jar with 1/4 cup Greek yogurt and 1 tbsp chia, and says at least 2 hours but overnight is creamier; its classic flavor adds vanilla, cinnamon and walnuts. Once Upon a Chef uses less yogurt, adds a pinch of salt and cinnamon and chills at least 4 hours, and Spend With Pennies layers fruit under and over the oats in the jars. This one follows the lead's base for four jars with blueberries and toasted walnuts on top.
